summary:
ASTRA is an intelligent astronaut health monitoring platform designed to support crew health and well-being during space missions. It brings physical health indicators, mental wellness monitoring, radiation exposure awareness, and AI-assisted health insights together in one interactive dashboard.

The platform monitors simulated astronaut health data, identifies potential anomalies, generates alerts, and presents health trends to support timely decision-making. It also includes health reports and mission-oriented monitoring features.

ASTRA aims to demonstrate how an integrated digital health monitoring system could help support astronaut safety, improve health awareness, and contribute to better-informed decisions during long-duration space missions. The current prototype uses simulated data and is not connected to live NASA systems.
details:
ASTRA – Astronaut Smart Tracking

Problem StatementAstronauts experience several physical and psychological challenges during space missions, including cardiovascular changes, muscle and bone deterioration, sleep disturbances, stress, and radiation exposure. Continuous awareness of these factors is important for supporting crew health, particularly during long-duration missions.Our SolutionASTRA is an interactive astronaut health monitoring platform that brings multiple health indicators into a unified dashboard. It is designed to demonstrate how digital monitoring and AI-assisted analysis can support astronaut health awareness.Key FeaturesIntegrated astronaut health dashboard.Cardiovascular and vital-sign monitoring.Physical health and musculoskeletal monitoring.Mental wellness and sleep monitoring.Radiation exposure awareness.Bio-Wellness Index visualization.AI-assisted health insights.Anomaly detection and alert generation.Health timeline and report generation.Re-settable demonstration baseline.How It WorksASTRA processes simulated astronaut health readings and displays them through interactive dashboards and monitoring views. When abnormal readings are introduced through demonstration scenarios, the platform illustrates how potential health anomalies can be highlighted through alerts and health insights.Expected ImpactASTRA aims to demonstrate a unified approach to astronaut health awareness, supporting mission teams with accessible health information and potential early identification of concerning trends.Future ScopeFuture development could include integration with validated biomedical sensors, real-time telemetry, scientifically validated health-risk models, and secure communication with mission medical support systems.Technical NoteThe current version is a software prototype using simulated data for demonstration. It is not connected to live NASA systems and is not a medical diagnostic tool.
